note: Adjudicated variants. One is orthographic rather than accidental: witness do sets the classical neglegéntiis, this edition and witness handmissal-eo the ecclesiastical negligéntiis. Both are the word; the letters differ; so it is ruled here rather than passed over, and collation counts it apart from the punctuation below.

adjudicated.ruling: Both spellings are real: neglegéntia is the classical form, negligéntia the later ecclesiastical one, and the dictionaries head both. The 1962 books of this recension print negligéntiis — handmissal-eo does on its printed page 10, and so does the Missale Romanum in its own Ordo — so the edition prints that, and records do's reading here rather than silently correcting a page that is not wrong.

No comma before the apposition 'Deo meo vivo et vero', with DO and with the corpus rulings at ordinarium.confiteor w064 and ordinarium.aufer-a-nobis w018: an apposition is not cut off from the word it restates. Editions differ here, and the hand missal's comma marks where a reader draws breath in a long sentence.
